summary: Round 5, a re-confirm after engine and catalog changes only (power_budget voltage drop, wire-end terminals). No part, project.yaml or DESIGN.md change. report.json has ok=true and no problems. All 10 requirements pass: power 0.143, torque_tilt 0.02 of 0.9, mass 59.3 g of 90, cam_clear 0.9 against 0.8, FEA peaks 1.1 to 2.6 MPa against 13 MPa, head_cg lateral 13.5 mm. WIRING.md and ASSEMBLY.md are consistent with the report, the assembly sheet still shows the same head, and nothing has regressed. The round-4 minor findings stand.

findings.issue: The 21T aluminium horn bolt circle, M2 thread and hub depth are catalog ESTIMATES, and the SG90 tab-hole position and shaft offset were scaled from a drawing. A wrong horn puts four bolt holes in the wrong place.
findings.fix: Measure the purchased horns and servos before printing. Print the base first as a test-fit coupon, and print the bracket's horn plate before the full part. Update the catalog if the numbers differ.

findings.issue: The pivot axial gap is 0.9 mm against a 0.8 mm cam_clear requirement, leaving only 0.1 mm of margin. Shrinkage or elephant's foot could bind the tilt.
findings.fix: After the first print, check the tilt by hand. If it is tight, shim or sand the knuckle and wall faces. Consider the 1.0 mm param max as the default.

findings.issue: The WIRING steps say to cut and solder jack -> servo, but an SG90 ships with its own 3-pin lead. The step 2 note mentions a 300 mm servo extension, but the connector and the rejoining of power and signal into one 3-pin plug are not specified or in bom_extra. The WIRING.md runs also show Avg A 0.00 for the signal runs and have no voltage-drop row.
findings.fix: State that the runs are two 300 mm 3-pin servo extensions with their pins split at the supply end, and add that cable to bom_extra.

findings.issue: The Pi's 3.3 V GPIO drives the SG90 signal pin directly with no series resistor. The common ground is only a note on the signal run (step 3).
findings.fix: Add a 330 ohm to 1 kohm series resistor on each signal line and a bolded common-ground step. Keep the 470-1000 uF cap at the jack.

findings.issue: 3.5% of the surface needs support, including the roofs of the 2.4 mm key-access holes and the M3 pilot, which are likely to sag.
findings.fix: Check the sliced preview and clean the holes with a 2.4 mm drill if needed.

findings.issue: The load axis Z runs across layers on all three parts (FEA SF is large). The yoke wall roots and the M2 tab pilots have the weakest layer orientation and will wear.
findings.fix: Use 5+ perimeters or 100% infill on the yoke walls. Re-tap or fit M2 heat-set inserts if the tab screws wear.

findings.issue: Several items are unpriced (servos, PSU, jack, Pi, camera, FPC, capacitor, USB supply). The horn price is about half the build cost, for parts whose geometry is estimated.
findings.fix: Add the prices and confirm the horn geometry before buying two horns.
